lines.t: In the land of sorrow, ashes on the ground,
A faithful man was tested, the silence was profound.
Riches turned to ruin, friends turned into doubt,
Still he whispered softly, “I will not curse or shout.”
The storm rolled in, the thunder cried,
But hope was burning deep inside.
Though the sky falls down and the night grows cold,
Still my heart will stand, still my soul will hold.
You give and take away, but my faith remains,
Through dust and pain, Your truth sustains.
Questions filled the heavens, cries filled the air,
Why must the righteous suffer, does Heaven even care?
But then came the voice, from the whirlwind’s flame,
“Were you there when I made the stars by name?”
The mountains bowed, the sea replied,
And Job beheld the Great Most High.
Though the sky falls down and the night grows cold,
Still my heart will stand, still my soul will hold.
You give and take away, but my faith remains,
Through dust and pain, Your truth sustains.
Now I see with open eyes,
Your purpose shining through disguise.
The end restored, the soul refined,
Your mercy endless, Your power divine.
Though the sky falls down and the night grows cold,
Still my heart will stand, still my soul will hold.
You give and take away, but I’ll still proclaim,
Forever You are holy—forever the same.
In the ashes, I have seen Your face,
My Redeemer lives, my heart finds grace.
